name: Projection Boundary Governance Registry
purpose: Formalize how indivisible recursive process relations may be projected into domain-specific symbolic layers without treating those projections as primitives.

core_rule.name: projection_not_primitive_rule
core_rule.definition: Any arithmetic-like, topology-like, geometry-like, QM-like, or GR-like expression derived from a process relation is a projection layer unless separately proven otherwise.

projection_domains.allowed_role: Symbolic simplification or counting of projected distinctions.
projection_domains.forbidden_role: Replacing standard arithmetic or claiming -1 = +1 numerically.

projection_domains.allowed_role: Representing bounded relation structure and admissibility neighborhoods.
projection_domains.forbidden_role: Inferring global topology or universal manifolds.

projection_domains.allowed_role: Representing stabilized continuation channels as projected constraint geometry.
projection_domains.forbidden_role: Claiming physical spacetime geometry is derived.

projection_domains.allowed_role: Representing threshold, discreteness, exclusion, participation, and local distinction behavior.
projection_domains.forbidden_role: Claiming quantum mechanics has been reformulated or proven.

projection_domains.allowed_role: Representing smooth continuation, propagation, and large-scale constraint flow analogies.
projection_domains.forbidden_role: Claiming general relativity has been derived or unified.

formal_seed.domain_index: D in {arithmetic_like, topology_like, geometry_like, QM_like, GR_like}
formal_seed.non_identity_rule: PI_D(WholeR) is not identical to WholeR.
formal_seed.loss_rule: Projection may lose residue-history, aspect simultaneity, or admissibility context.
formal_seed.traceability_rule: Each projection must retain a recoverable pointer to the originating process relation.
formal_seed.boundary_rule: No projection may be promoted to primitive status without separate governance.

allowed_uses: Mapping process relations into domain-specific symbolic language.
Comparing different projections of the same recursive relation.
Explaining why arithmetic-like or physics-like expressions remain analogical.
Preventing projection artifacts from being mistaken for primitives.
forbidden_uses: Treating projected arithmetic as replacement arithmetic.
Treating projected geometry as physical spacetime.
Treating QM-like and GR-like projections as a completed unification.
Treating any projection as proof of the primitive relation.
Dropping residue-history without recording projection loss.
Using projection language to bypass theorem obligations.
